name: Outer case
description: Holds the electronics and supports the switch plate. Eight thin windows around its perimeter let the LEDs shine through.
spec: 110 × 110 × 25 mm; print open side up. Frosted clear PETG is suitable.
note: Print this part in clear PETG.

name: Switch plate v5
description: Upper switch plate with four underside bosses for hidden tray screws. The joystick area is flat and accepts a separate keyed adapter; only the four corner case screws remain on the front.
spec: 94 × 94 mm; 3 mm main plate. Four 8 mm diameter bosses extend 9 mm below it. Two 4 mm joystick locating holes, two 2.4 mm screw holes and an aligned wire slot.
note: Both full plates change in v5. Print the four small test pieces first. Upper visible face DOWN, bosses UP. Heat-set inserts go in the underside bosses, not the lower tray.

name: Round foot
description: Supports the case on the desk. Its underside has recessed screw seats and its top has pockets for optional steel weights.
spec: 84 mm diameter × 5 mm tall. Add adhesive rubber below.
note: Print this part in white PETG.

name: Removable joystick adapter v5
description: A separate flat adapter supports the joystick and both mounting tabs. Two solid underside pegs locate it in the top plate; screws clamp through all three layers into exposed nuts.
spec: 21.81 × 24.52 mm footprint; 1.6 mm base, 0.5/1.0 mm raised ear seats. 3.6 mm pegs in 4 mm holes. M1.6 × 10 screws required.
note: Print adapter pegs DOWN with support under its base. Test with the corner sample before printing the full plate. Reuse the tested adapter. No nut boxes or loose shims; physical fit pending.

name: Touch cap
description: The fixed cap you touch to change input banks. A copper disk immediately underneath its thin top surface acts as the sensor.
spec: 0.8 mm sensing skin; 13 mm copper disk underneath. This is not a push button.
note: Print this part in black PETG.

name: Dial knob
description: Fits over the rotary encoder’s D-shaped shaft, making it easy to turn and press.
spec: 6.2 mm nominal D socket. Test fit and allow clearance for the encoder click.
note: Print this part in white PETG.

name: Lower light tray v5 (test samples first)
description: Six light compartments with 10 × 4 mm access openings. Four short mounting shelves receive screws from below; the heat-set inserts now live in the upper plate.
spec: 91 × 45.325 × 12 mm; black PETG. M3 × 8 screws point upward through 3.4 mm clearance holes.
note: Use only with the matching v5 upper plate. New upper and lower samples required. Four tray inserts install in the upper plate; two extra inserts stay in the sample. LEDs need thin insulating tape and wiring slack.

name: Translucent agent keycap
description: Lets each agent’s status light show through while providing a normal mechanical key surface.
spec: Flat finger surface, rounded corners and 0.5 mm beveled rim. Standard MX cross socket. Print a stem-fit coupon first; purchased caps are an option.
note: Print this part in clear PETG. Top UP; start with 0.10–0.12 mm layers on a 0.4 mm nozzle. Support the underside as needed and keep the sockets clear. Print a stem-fit coupon and one cap first.

name: White command keycap
description: Covers the individual command switches. The supplied legend sheet adds labels for Fast, approve, decline, new chat and send.
spec: Flat finger surface, rounded corners and 0.5 mm beveled rim. Same 1U CAD as the agent cap; use white filament.
note: Print this part in white PETG. Top UP; start with 0.10–0.12 mm layers on a 0.4 mm nozzle. Support the underside as needed and keep the sockets clear. Print a stem-fit coupon and one cap first.

name: Wide microphone keycap
description: Presses two independent switches together. The firmware combines those switch events into one logical key.
spec: Flat finger surface, rounded corners and 0.5 mm beveled rim. Two MX sockets, 19.05 mm apart. A conventional centered 2U cap will not fit.
note: Print this part in white PETG. Top UP; start with 0.10–0.12 mm layers on a 0.4 mm nozzle. Support the underside as needed and keep the sockets clear. Print a stem-fit coupon and one cap first.

name: Switch-fit coupon
description: Tests three hole sizes before you spend time printing the full switch plate.
spec: 14.0, 14.1 and 14.2 mm openings. Pick a snug clip fit without forcing.
note: Print this part in white PETG.

name: Stem and insert coupon
description: Tests keycap cross sockets and the heat-set insert hole before printing final parts.
spec: Three stem allowances and a 3.9 mm insert pilot. Also print in the cap material when testing stems.
note: Print this part in clear PETG.

name: Adafruit KB2040
description: The USB-C microcontroller reads every control and drives the LEDs. It runs the supplied CircuitPython prototype firmware.
spec: 35 × 17.8 × 4.9 mm envelope. USB only; no Bluetooth.
note: Generic USB macros and manual RGBW control are implemented. Native Codex integration is not.

name: Gateron North Pole Yellow 2.0
description: Mechanical key switches. Transparent upper and lower housings let the agent LEDs shine through. Two switches sit under the wide cap.
spec: Normal MX, 5-pin type; not Choc or Hall-effect. Seller pack: 35.

name: Thumb slide joystick
description: A flat analog joystick that reads horizontal and vertical movement. The prototype firmware converts this into arrow-key actions.
spec: SparkFun COM-09426 / PSP1000 style. Power from 3.3 V; check pad orientation.
note: Test the actual joystick on the v5 removable adapter and corner sample. Confirm both tabs rest on their supports without bending and full travel is free.

name: Rotary encoder with push switch
description: Reads dial rotation and clicks. The prototype maps these to scrolling and Enter.
spec: Adafruit 377; 6 mm D shaft, M7 panel bushing. Nut and washer included.

name: Encoder nut and washer
description: Clamps the rotary encoder to the switch plate without relying on its electrical pins.
spec: Included with the specified encoder. Tighten gently against plastic.

name: Mini RGBW NeoPixel board
description: Individually addressable light boards: six illuminate agent keys and eight face outward through the case.
spec: Adafruit 4776; 9.1 × 9.1 × 3.1 mm. Buy two packs of ten. GRBW firmware order.
note: Power from fused RAW/5 V through a shared ground. Firmware limits brightness to 15%.

name: 74AHCT125 level shifter
description: Converts the controller’s 3.3 V LED data signal into a reliable 5 V signal for the pixel chain.
spec: DIP package, 5 V supply. Follow the wiring diagram for unused gates and enable pins.

name: 1N4148 signal diode
description: One per switch prevents false key events when multiple keys are pressed together.
spec: Band faces the matrix row. Buy two packs of ten.

name: Silicone hookup wire
description: Connects the switch matrix, controls, controller and light chain. Leave enough slack to lift the plate for service.
spec: 28 AWG for signals; use 24–26 AWG for the power trunk. Insulate crossings.

name: Copper touch electrode
description: Senses a finger through the thin plastic touch cap. Solder its lead before attaching it beneath the cap.
spec: 13 mm copper disk; D10 with a 1 MΩ resistor to ground.

name: 3 mm indicator LED
description: Shows which of the three prototype macro banks is selected. Each needs its own series resistor.
spec: 3 mm LED; 1 kΩ resistor per LED.

name: Resistors and capacitors
description: Limit current, stabilize the LED supply, and make the touch and data connections work correctly.
note: Select the listed values. This is a catalog link, not a preassembled kit.

name: Small prototype circuit board
description: Supports the level shifter and small passive components in the front bay of the case.
spec: Trim to at most 25 × 20 mm. Insulate the underside.

name: M3 heat-set insert
description: Metal threads in printed plastic: four for the case, two for the foot and four underneath the v5 UPPER plate for the lower light tray. Two additional inserts stay in the upper test sample.
spec: 4.2 mm outside diameter × 4 mm long. Starting pilot: 3.9 mm. Test coupon first.
note: Use spares from the existing Adafruit 50-pack. Test heat-set fit before printing the full tray.

name: M3 × 8 mm plate screw
description: Fastens the switch plate to the four corner inserts in the case.
spec: M3 × 8 mm socket-head screw. Do not overtighten.

name: Low-profile M3 × 8 mm screw
description: Attaches the foot from underneath while keeping the head recessed.
spec: Head at most 6 mm wide and 1.7 mm tall. Choose low-profile heads.

name: Steel weight washer
description: Adds a little weight so the keypad feels steadier on the desk. Tape the washers into the round foot’s top pockets.
spec: M8 oversized washer, 316 stainless steel, 8.4 mm inside diameter, 24 mm outside diameter, nominal 2 mm thick.
note: One pack covers the four optional weights. McMaster specifies 1.8–2.2 mm thickness; check your printed pockets and allow room for the retaining tape before assembly.

name: Adhesive rubber feet
description: Keeps the keypad from sliding and protects the desk. Attach beneath the printed foot.
spec: 1–2 mm thick adhesive rubber. No TPU printing is required.

name: USB-C data cable
description: Powers the controller and LEDs and carries keyboard, mouse and serial data to the computer.
spec: Must support data. Connector overmold must fit the 15 × 8 mm case tunnel.

name: Insulation and mounting tape
description: Insulates solder joints and secures the controller and optional weights. LED mounting tape is listed separately.
spec: Polyimide tape plus thin removable foam tape. About 1.6 mm below the controller.

name: LED mounting tape — 3M 9474LE
description: Holds the mini LED boards in the printed tray pockets. Cut small pieces from a sheet; one pack is more than enough for this keyboard.
spec: 3M 9474LE with 300LSE adhesive and a polyester film carrier. 0.17 mm thick excluding the peel-off liners; sheets are 12 × 9.5 inches.
note: Use one layer within the tray’s 0.2 mm adhesive allowance. Keep LED faces and wire openings clear. Strong permanent adhesive: dry-fit and test the light before sticking it down.

name: Clear key-label decal paper
description: Adds the command symbols to your blank white printed keycaps. Use the supplied SVG legend sheet.
spec: Optional. Match inkjet or laser paper to your printer; follow its sealing instructions.

name: Clear PETG
description: Filament for the case and six agent keycaps. These are material allowances, not slicer estimates.
spec: 0.4 mm nozzle starting point; 0.20 mm layers, finer for caps. Verify your printer’s filament diameter.
note: Choose colorless clear PETG for light transmission. Frosted is fine; optical clarity is not required.

name: White PETG
description: Filament for the plate, command caps, knob and foot. These are material allowances, not slicer estimates.
spec: 0.4 mm nozzle starting point; 0.20 mm layers, finer for caps. Verify your printer’s filament diameter.

name: Black PETG
description: Filament for the light baffles, touch cap and joystick cradle. These are material allowances, not slicer estimates.
spec: 0.4 mm nozzle starting point; 0.20 mm layers, finer for caps. Verify your printer’s filament diameter.

name: Creator Micro 2 Pro
description: A genuine supported device is the documented route to native Codex controls, live task colors and Bluetooth. Keep its controller and firmware.
spec: The supplied custom case is not a verified donor fit. Measure the board and revise mounts before printing.
note: Alternative to a genuine Codex Micro, not an additional purchase. Check seller availability.

name: Genuine Codex Micro
description: The original OpenAI × Work Louder device. It has the native integration, factory light diffuser, battery and mechanical assembly.
spec: Alternative to Creator Micro 2 Pro. It was listed out of stock during the original research.

name: Frosted MX Pure caps
description: Optional frosted caps for a genuine Creator Micro 2 so the six agent lights remain visible.
spec: Keep genuine electronics and diffuser. Check the seller’s compatibility and shipping status.

name: Joystick M1.6 × 10 mm screws — v5
description: Two longer screws pass downward through the joystick tabs, separate adapter and top plate. The previous 8 mm screws are too short for full nut engagement in this stack.
spec: DIN 912; 0.35 mm pitch; 3 mm head diameter; 1.5 mm hex drive.
note: New length for v5; reuse the existing M1.6 nuts. Check seller availability and pack quantity. 1.5 mm hex key.

name: Joystick M1.6 hex nuts
description: Tighten against the flat underside of the v5 upper plate. Hold these exposed nuts with small pliers while gently turning the M1.6 × 10 screws from above.
spec: DIN 934; 3.2 mm across flats; 1.3 mm thick.
note: Check supplier availability and pack quantity before ordering. No new electronics required.

name: Baffle tray screws — reuse M3 × 8 mm
description: Four spare case-type screws enter upward from underneath the lower tray and thread into inserts in the upper plate. No tray screw heads on the front.
spec: M3 × 8 mm under-head length; McMaster 91290A113 socket head. 2.5 mm hex key.
note: Use spares from your existing pack; do not remove case screws. No M3 × 20 screws or loose tray nuts needed.
